why: “In your Command phase, select one Throttlerokkit Shokka Engine ability. This unit has that ability until the start of your next Command phase.” Selection is your Command phase; the abilities it can give take effect in your Command phase (Shokk Attack Engine: “In your Command phase”), your Movement phase (Pulse Jet: “In your Movement phase”; Turbo Engine: advance/fall-back moves, which core 09.02 lists as Movement-phase move types) and your Charge phase (Turbo Engine: “eligible to declare a charge”). None of them can act in the opponent’s turn, so “your” is right.

“When this unit is selected to make an advance/fall-back move, that move does not prevent this unit from being eligible to declare a charge.” Advance and fall-back moves are move types of the Movement phase (core 09.02, active player), and the eligibility matters when declaring a charge (11.02, “It made an advance or fall-back move this turn”). Your Movement and Charge phases are exactly where it acts.

New Recruit prints Turbo Engine under the heading “Throttlerokkit Shokka Engine”, and Full Throttle says “select one Throttlerokkit Shokka Engine ability”; “pick one” is a shorter “select one”. The when and how long stay on the Full Throttle row. Model line is NR’s “1x Wazdakka Gutsmek”.

“In your Movement phase, when this unit is selected to move … this unit can make a pulse jet move.” The text names your Movement phase. (For the owner: the lasting effects, “Until the end of the turn … not eligible to declare a charge” and “Until the start of your next turn, attacks that target your unit have -1 to hit rolls”, are in the Pulse Jet Move rule, not in this ability’s words, so the tag doesn’t carry them.)

“If this unit made a charge move this turn, this model’s melee attacks have +3 A, +2 S.” Melee attacks are made in the Fight phase, and a charge move can happen in either turn (your Charge phase, or Heroic Intervention in theirs: “Resolve a charge with your unit”), so Fight in either turn.

“That VEHICLE model’s attacks have +1 to hit rolls until the start of your next Movement phase.” The effect lasts through your Shooting phase, your Fight phase and the opponent’s whole turn, so it takes effect wherever the picked VEHICLE model attacks: your Shooting phase and the Fight phase of either turn. The tag lists only the Movement phase, where the pick and “heals D3 wounds” happen. Nothing in this list lets a VEHICLE shoot in their Shooting phase, and no attacks are made in a Charge or Command phase. Their Movement phase is left out because its only attacks are Fire Overwatch, and snap shooting “only hits on an unmodified hit roll of 6 (irrespective of … any modifiers)”. If the owner wants the convention the app uses for Spiteful Power Trip (listing Overwatch), make movement “either”. The per-phase “turns” override is the app’s own field (data.js: “turns:{ phase:turn } overrides it for one phase”).

No unit in this list changes (all are Faction: Orks), but the filter should copy the text’s keywords. The when (“Picked by a Mek’s Clever Know-wotz”) and the note (“that VEHICLE model’s attacks have +1 to hit rolls until the start of your next Movement phase”) are literal. (The Dreadherder aura’s needs {all:[Walker]} for “friendly ORKS WALKER unit” has the same gap. It is not in this batch.)

Text: “Friendly ORKS INFANTRY units’ ranged attacks have: [ASSAULT]. While this unit is riled up, +3" R.” No phase or turn limit. With turn “either” and turns {shooting:your}, the tag reads Movement (either turn) / Your Shooting. Two problems. (1) It leaves out their Shooting phase. Gun-crazy Show-offs, a Wreckas stratagem in this list, says “WHEN: Your opponent’s Shooting phase … Your unit shoots using normal shooting” for a FLASH GITZ/TANKBUSTAS unit, and those are ORKS INFANTRY: their ranged attacks have [ASSAULT] and, if riled up (Intimidating Motivation: “riled up until the start of your next turn”), +3" R. (2) It includes your own Movement phase, where no ranged attacks are made. The Movement entry is for Fire Overwatch (“End of your opponent’s Movement phase”), which is their turn. With rule-turn “either”, the fix gives Their Movement / Shooting (either turn).
